subject.title: [Bug]: Assistant text preceding a tool call in the same turn is silently dropped on Signal channel (Anthropic/Sonnet, non-streaming)

question: For `stopReason:"toolUse"` assistant text that precedes a tool call, should OpenClaw deliver it automatically to messaging channels, or suppress it while making the suppression explicit to the agent/session state?
rationale: The reported bug is real delivery-state drift, but related open work asks to suppress intermediate tool text to avoid channel leaks; automation should not pick the permanent visibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Surface suppression to the agent
options.body: Keep intermediate pre-tool text out of channels unless it is intentionally deliverable, but annotate/session-signal the suppression so the agent cannot assume the user saw it.

options.title: Deliver pre-tool text before tools
options.body: Flush pre-tool text to the channel before executing the tool, accepting the risk that some intermediate narration becomes visible.

options.title: Require explicit send semantics
options.body: Move messaging-channel visibility toward final text or message-tool sends only, with docs and regression coverage for transcript/client consistency.

recommendation.title: Surface suppression to the agent
recommendation.body: Keep intermediate pre-tool text out of channels unless it is intentionally deliverable, but annotate/session-signal the suppression so the agent cannot assume the user saw it.

likelyOwner.reason: The current incomplete-turn and payload-selection code most directly connected to the policy is in recent commits by this author.
